label: Fed-back first token f at copy step 2 (recall_idx 1) in long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at the step right after <DEL> + first output (recall_idx == 1), when the fed-back input is f, i.e. the sequence starts with f. About 99% of activation mass is in_tok f, and nearly all of it is at recall_idx 1 with prev_tok <DEL>. Gated by length: silent for L <= 5, weak and partial at L = 6 (about 40% of f-start L=6 sequences, low-quartile magnitudes), reliable for L >= 7, and mass grows with L (L=9 has the largest share). Does not fire in the original or delimiter phases, on f at later copy steps, or on other tokens (a few stray hits on e, 1, z, c). Magnitude does not depend on the token being output (out_tok, next_out flat). Adding L>=6 instead of L>=7 raises recall to 0.98 but lowers precision to 0.85.

issues: The only systematic miss class is L=6, f-initial, recall_idx 1. It is weak: it holds about 1.5% of mass and all of it is in the low quartile, and the explanation already documents it. Firing there is not determined by the variables tested. With L==6 alone the predicate has precision 0.43 on test, and adding it lowers F1 to 0.916, so the L>=7 cutoff is justified.
Stray hits are negligible. At recall_idx 2 with in_tok f, precision is 0.004 (0.7% of active steps). At recall_idx 1 with in_tok not f, precision is 0.0002 (0.8% of active steps).

Phase, L, recall_idx, prev_tok=<DEL> and the flat out_tok profile all match the profile. The test split reproduces the reported scores: P 0.9999, R 0.862, F1 0.926, mass recall 0.984. There is 1 false positive.
